body.x: Luchrome, a pioneering French startup specializing in next-generation connected electronics displays, announced that it will unveil its proprietary ultra-low-power display platform, Lusight, at CES 2026, held from January 6 to 9 in Las Vegas, United States.

Founded in 2023, Luchrome has focused on developing display technologies that dramatically reduce energy consumption and improve how humans and machines communicate. The company received strong validation from the global technology community after being selected as a winner of the prestigious CES Innovation Award in the Sustainability & Energy Transition category, a recognition reserved for only a small fraction of applicants.

The award-winning platform Lusight represents a major shift in electronic display philosophy. Unlike conventional displays that require constant high power and complex integration, Lusight was engineered as a modular system that can be easily embedded in any connected object. According to Luchrome, the platform consumes up to ten times less power than current displays, making it suitable for truly autonomous, battery-efficient, and sustainable devices.

After years of research and development, the Lusight platform is now entering its final qualification phase. Luchrome explained that the technology will be available for pre-order starting in 2026, following qualification, and that commercial availability will begin with industry-focused showcases scheduled from March 2026.

CEO Romain Futsch emphasized the broader vision behind the debut. “With Lusight, we are reinventing electronic displays to address the energy and technological challenges of tomorrow. IFA 2025 and CES 2026 are not just exhibition participations for us, but important stages where we demonstrate Made in France responsible innovation to global buyers, partners, and consumers,” he said.

At CES 2026, Luchrome will conduct live demonstrations at Booth 60412 in the French Pavilion at Eureka Park, Hall G, Venetian Expo Center, presenting interactive Lusight experiences and diverse real-world applications. The company aims to showcase how Lusight can be applied to healthcare, industrial automation, logistics equipment, and consumer electronics markets worldwide.

Luchrome stated that CES 2026 will serve as a strategic launchpad for international collaboration. Through engagement with global media journalists, investors, and advanced-industry buyers, the company plans to expand API integration partnerships and propose a new global standard for energy-efficient human-machine interfaces.

The company also expressed gratitude to its ecosystem supporters. Luchrome thanked TeamNAqui, the Nouvelle-Aquitaine Region, CCI International, La French Tech, Business France, and the broader French technology ecosystem for their continued sponsorship and technical support, which enabled the company’s presence on the CES stage.
